subject: ClinicalEdge — evaluation specs & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@clinicaledge.com>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@clinicaledge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: ClinicalEdge — evaluation specs & next steps

Hi Emma / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the call today — good alignment on the use cases (discharge-summary compression + structured problem-list extraction). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get an apples-to-apples baseline on Redwood: 

What we heard (goal):
- Produce concise, clinically accurate discharge summaries and a structured problem-list per patient.
- Measure factuality and medical-entity fidelity (low hallucination).
- Baseline cost/latency comparisons across 2–3 candidate models and recommend a production profile.

Our recommended baseline models to evaluate (fast iteration -> production options):
1) redwood-instruct-2.7b (fp16) — low-cost baseline for throughput testing
2) redwood-13b-quant (q4_0) — mid-point for quality/latency tradeoff
3) redwood-instruct-70b (server-side) — optional upper-bound quality test (longer latency)

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) You share 1–2 sample datasets (<= 2k records total) — we can run a baseline within 48 business hours. Please attach as CSV or JSONL.
2) We run an initial eval using our eval harness (metrics: exact-match for structured fields, token-level F1 for free-text, ROUGE-L, and a hallucination metric tied to medical-entity overlap).
3) Redwood SE (Marissa) will provide a runnable eval template + prompts and a short CLI example to run locally or via our Console.
4) Align on success thresholds and follow with a 1-week focused eval comparing the two preferred models.

Security & data handling: if data contains PHI, please indicate. For PHI workflows we recommend using Redwood Private or a dedicated S3 bucket with customer-managed keys.

Attachments included: sample eval template (redwood_eval_template.jsonl) — this has the expected field list and scorer config.

Proposed calendar: SE deep-dive on Feb 12 (30 minutes) to finalize dataset format and scoring. Does 14:00–14:30 PT work for you?

Thanks — I’ll stand up the baseline job as soon as I have the sample files.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Ben — this looks great. A few clarifying Qs before we send the full sample: 

1) Scoring: can you confirm the exact metrics and thresholds you plan to report? For our clinical QA team we need clear thresholds for: problem-list entity precision/recall, overall hallucination rate, and a user-facing summary accuracy score.
2) PHI & de-id: the sample I’m attaching is de-identified but will still contain free-text notes. Is that acceptable? If not, we need guidance on de-id.
3) Format: we can attach a CSV (columns below). Does Redwood prefer JSONL over CSV for the eval harness?

We attached "clinicaledge_sample_dataset_v1.csv" (10 records) — columns: patient_id, encounter_id, discharge_note, gold_summary, gold_problem_list (pipe-delimited).

We can do Feb 12 at 14:00 PT for the SE session. Also looping in Alex (CTO) for procurement timing/questions on the 70b test cost.

Best,
Emma Johnson

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@clinicaledge.com>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@clinicaledge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 12:38:02 -0800
Subject: Re: ClinicalEdge — evaluation specs & next steps

Thanks Emma — attaching a short tech note below and the eval template you can drop your CSV into. (High-level — we’ll walk through details on the Feb 12 call.)

Quick answers:
- Preferred format: JSONL is the most straightforward for our harness (one JSON object per line). CSV is fine — we will convert it during ingestion but JSONL avoids ambiguity around nested fields like problem_list.
- Required schema (JSONL accepted fields):
  * id (string) — unique record id
  * input_text (string) — full discharge note or concatenated context
  * prompt (string) — the instruction/prompt used for generation (optional if using a single prompt across dataset)
  * expected (string) — gold summary (free text) or a serialized structured object (pipe-delimited list OK)
  * metadata (string) — free-form metadata (e.g., encounter_date, deid_flag)

Scoring criteria (what we will compute in the baseline report):
- Structured fields (problem-list): precision / recall / F1 using exact-match on normalized medical entities (token normalization + UMLS-backed mapping where possible).
- Free-text summary: ROUGE-L and token-level F1 against the gold_summary.
- Hallucination metric: entity-level false-positive rate (entities present in generated output but not in gold) normalized per 1k tokens.
- Overall "Quality" score: weighted composite (0–100) we’ll show; weights are configurable but default to 50% structure F1, 30% ROUGE-L, 20% hallucination_penalty.

Evaluation steps on Redwood (CLI + Console examples):
1) Upload dataset (JSONL) to your S3 bucket or share via Drive link. If you use S3, please give read-only path and we will import directly.
2) Create eval job via Console: "Create -> Eval" then pick dataset and models.
   OR CLI: redwood eval create --name "clin-edge-baseline" --dataset s3://clinicaledge-evals/clinicaledge_v1.jsonl --models redwood-instruct-2.7b,redwood-13b-quant --scorer default-clinical --output s3://redwood-outputs/rdw-clin-0421/
3) Scorer config: use the attached redwood_eval_template.jsonl to set which metrics to compute. The template contains the scorer id "default-clinical" and example threshold configs.
4) Expected runtime: small datasets (<=2k records) typically complete in 2–6 hours per model depending on batch size. We’ll attach token-cost estimates in the report.

Prompt examples (we’ll include these in the template but here are two to test):
- Instructional (single-shot): "Summarize the following discharge note into a 3–4 sentence concise summary suitable for a primary care follow-up. Also return a pipe-delimited problem-list of active diagnoses."
- Structured extraction prompt: "List the active problems and the recommended plan for each problem from the note below. Output as: PROBLEM|PLAN on separate lines."

On PHI: if records are de-identified you’re fine to upload. If not, please request a Private eval (we can run within your VPC) — Ben can advise on an SOW for Private/secure runs.

If you want, we can pre-configure the 13b quant job and post the baseline report to the Drive folder we listed. I’ll also include a short example of scorer output in the Drive folder before the call.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
